confirmed.title: Day off keeps no morning free: morningFree is 0, design and doc say 06:00 (360), so days off lose their second local night
confirmed.specItem: R: days off = Directive 2000/79/EC 'single day free of duty' (1 day + 2 local nights); recurrent extended recovery rest of 36 h incl. 2 local nights (ORO.FTL.235(d)); UPDATE-0.9.md §R 'free of all duty, standby and reserve from 00:00 to 06:00 the next morning', BAL `morningFree: 360`
confirmed.evidence: balance.ts:402 `off: { legalMonth: 7, minMonth: 8, targetMonth: 9, maxMonth: 10, yearMin: 96, block: [2, 3], dueAfter: 5, mustAfter: 6, morningFree: 0 }` while docs/acmi/UPDATE-0.9.md:655 specifies `morningFree: 360` and :504 'from 00:00 to 06:00 the next morning (which keeps both local nights free)'; EASA-FTL.md §16 repeats the 06:00 definition. Consumers: dayPlan.ts:92 `const a = dayIndex(c.base, start - R().off.morningFree)` (a 05:00 report no longer takes the day off before), dayPlan.ts:962 `if (offOn(c, X - 1)) a = Math.max(a, m + S.off.morningFree)` with rawWindow's early shift `S.home.early = [300, 1020]` so the planner itself puts a 05:00 home standby right after every block of days off; rules.ts:371-377 nightsIn needs 8 h inside 22:00–08:00, so 22:00–05:00 (7 h) is not a local night. Effect: the last day of every off block is not a 'single day free of duty'; the single-day fallback (dayPlan.ts:694-697 'a single day off (1 day and 2 local nights) keeps the count') never has 2 nights; a 2-day block preceded by a duty ending after 00:00 (late finish) and followed by the 05:00 standby holds only one local night and is no recovery rest at all, so the 168 h clock keeps running and later duties fail 'recovery' (evalSegs rules.ts:677). Code comments (dayPlan.ts:299-300 'a 05:00 report takes the day off before's morning too') assume the 360.
confirmed.fix: Set `morningFree: 360` as designed. With it, planStandby starts the window after a day off at 06:00 (clip the early shift) and offDaysHit takes the day before a report earlier than 06:00; add a dayPlan.test assertion that every planned off block has ≥ 2 local nights (nightsIn(base, workEndBefore, nextWorkStart) ≥ 2) and that a single day off is 1 day + 2 nights.
verifier: HOLDS: Confirmed in code: src/engine/core/balance.ts:402 has `morningFree: 0` (so from the first WIP commit eb163ed; 360 never existed in git), while docs/acmi/UPDATE-0.9.md:655 specifies 360 and :504 defines a day off as free 'from 00:00 to 06:00 the next morning'. Consumers behave as the finding says: dayPlan.ts:962 `if (offOn(c, X - 1)) a = Math.max(a, m + S.off.morningFree)` with `home.early = [300, 1020]` (balance.ts:404) lets planStandby open a 05:00 home window the morning after every off block (nothing else clips it: `ready` only comes from restUntil/seg rest, and 2-day blocks pass windowIssues' recovery test), and offDaysHit (dayPlan.ts:92) / busyDays.hit (dayPlan.ts:360-369) let a report before 06:00 skip the day off before, contrary to takeOffDays' own comment (dayPlan.ts:299-300). One part of the finding is wrong and the severity is overstated: a 2- or 3-day block always holds >= 2 local nights even with 0 (the night before the first off day is free from at least 00:00, since any work ending after midnight hits that day via dayIndex(end-1), plus the full night between the off days), so days off do still qualify as 36 h recovery and the 'recovery illegal' consequence does not occur. The real defect is the planner breaking the doc's 00:00-06:00 definition; medium rather than high.

confirmed.title: Discretion applied at the gate leaves d.fdp at the planned value: the ORO.FTL.205(f)(5) authority report never files and gauges/log understate the day
confirmed.specItem: U (ORO.FTL.205(f)(5) report over 1 h; EASA-FTL.md §5 'Over 1 h at release: one inbox note')
confirmed.evidence: fdpOver(): `const fdp = g.now + Math.max(f.block, last.sta - f.std) - d.report; if (fdp <= d.maxFdp + (d.discretion ?? 0)) return false; if (!d.discretion) { const r = applyDiscretion(g, d.id, fdp); ... if (fdp <= d.maxFdp + (d.discretion ?? 0)) return false; } d.fdp = fdp;` — d.fdp is written only on the still-illegal path. A gate hold is `holdFlight`: `f.delay += min; schedule(...)` with no `f.ev++`, so `onFlightsChanged`/`syncDuty` (the only other writer of d.fdp, roster.ts:1009 `if (keep.length === d.flightIds.length && ev === d.flightsEv) continue;`) never re-measures the duty; arrival (`onFlightArr`) sets f.ata without an ev bump. Release then uses the stale value: index.ts:220 `const over = d.fdp - (d.ext && d.basicFdp ? d.basicFdp : d.maxFdp); if (d.discretion && over > 60) pushMessage(... 'Discretion report filed' ...)`, and timeline.ts:441 `let fdp = d.fdp + early` feeds c.log. Because v0.9 only allows discretion when plannedFdp ≤ maxFdp, d.fdp ≤ maxFdp at that moment, so `over` is ≤ 0 for every hold that stays inside the leg's block (ripple only when `f.sta <= g.now + min`, i.e. the hold exceeds the whole block time).
confirmed.fix: In fdpOver set `d.fdp = fdp` (and `d.legality = dutyLegality(d)`) on the `r.ok` branch too, or re-measure at release (`onBlocks(lastF) - d.report`) before the (f)(5) check and the log entry. Then the inbox note can also say the amount ('extends it by 0:40').
verifier: HOLDS: Confirmed in code. flights.ts:716-738 fdpOver writes d.fdp only after the `if (!d.discretion) {...}` block returns false on the ok path (line 733 `return false` before line 735 `d.fdp = fdp`). The only other writer is duties.ts:284 syncDuty, reached from roster.ts:1009 only when a flight's ev changed; holdFlight (flights.ts:66-72) and the delayChain `holdable` branch (flights.ts:327-336) add to f.delay and re-schedule with the same f.ev, so no re-sync happens. onFlightArr (flights.ts:1109+) sets ata without an ev bump, onDutyRelease (crew/index.ts:156-226) reads d.fdp directly at line 220 for the (f)(5) check and logs seg.fdp = d.fdp + early (timeline.ts:441) at line 194. Reachable sequence: last leg of a reported duty, slack 50 min; a 45-min ops delay is `holdable` (d.fdp+45 <= max) so it is a hold; an AOG then adds holdFlight 30 twice and a short fix is again `holdable` because holdable adds only the newest increment to the stale d.fdp; at departure fdpOver projects planned+135 min, discretion is applied (over 1:25 <= 2:00) and d.fdp stays at the planned value, so `over` at release is negative and no report files although the real overrun is over 1 h. plausible.title: Legal 7-days-off floor is pro-rated by training days although training is duty
plausible.specItem: R: at least 7 free days per calendar month (Directive 2000/79/EC); ORO.FTL.105(10) duty includes training; dayPlan.ts' own rule 'training is work' (resets())
plausible.evidence: dayPlan.ts:218-224 `export function legalFor(c, mk) { … for (let k = a; k < b; k++) if (blockOn(c, k)) away++; return Math.ceil((R().off.legalMonth * (b - a - away)) / (b - a)); }` and blockOn (dayPlan.ts:377-383) returns `x.why` for every block kind including `'training'`; minFor (dayPlan.ts:209-215) does the same. dayPlan.ts:385-386 `/** Leave, sickness and joining reset the work-day count; training is work. */ const resets = (w) => w === 'leave' || w === 'sick' || w === 'joining'` already treats training as work. A crew member on a 3-week conversion course gets a legal floor of ceil(7×9/30) = 3 days off; monthFloorIssue (line 170) and dayPlanMonth's monthsLow (line 1165) then accept 3–4 days off as legal.
plausible.fix: Count only blocks for which `resets(why)` is true (leave, sick, joining) as `away` in legalFor and minFor; training days stay inside the 7/8.
verifier: HOLDS: Confirmed: legalFor (dayPlan.ts:218-224) and minFor (:209-215) count `blockOn(c, k)` days as `away`, and blockOn (:377-383) returns `x.why` for all four kinds including 'training'; the function's own comment says 'pro rata in a month partly on leave, sick or joining' and dayPlan.ts:385-386 declares 'training is work' (resets() excludes it). Training blocks are real and sizeable: hr.ts:162-168 writes `{ why: 'training' }` for a command upgrade of 42 days (balance.ts:62), a pilot conversion of 14 days and a cabin conversion of 5 days (balance.ts:65), SCCM 4 days. A month with a 5-day cabin conversion gets a legal floor of ceil(7*25/30) = 6 and a 14-day conversion a floor of 4, which monthFloorIssue (:170-176) then accepts when placing work, while crewMonth (:1255) shows the player 'days off 6 of 7 minimum'. blockedMonth (:1170-1174) only stops dayPlanMonth counting months with > 10 such days; it does not touch the placement floor. Directive 2000/79/EC's 7 free days apply regardless of training, so the rule is mis-encoded for the partial-month case; medium is right.

REFUTED: The game models a course (conversion.ts:320, hr.ts:168) as one contiguous block with no days off inside it, and blockedOn forbids planning a day off on a training day. Counting training days as in-month would make the 7 unreachable during a 3-week course: monthFloorIssue would flag every fresh duty 'daysOff' illegal and dayPlanMonth would count monthsLow for crew the planner cannot give days to. The proposed fix is worse than the current pro-rating unless training blocks also get days off inside them, which the finding does not propose; the pro-rating is the same treatment the design gives leave and sickness ('a month partly on leave, sick or joining').

plausible.title: Standby, extension and time-zone issues are mis-named as the FDP or minimum-rest limit on the card
plausible.evidence: LIMIT_OF: `fdp: 'fdp', ext7d: 'fdp', standby: 'fdp', rest: 'rest', lateEarly: 'rest', tzRest: 'rest'`. A 'standby' issue ('On standby from 05:00: more than 18 h awake by the end of the day', rules.ts:634–637) is reported as 'the day-length limit (FDP)'; 'ext7d' ('Already 2 extended days this week') as the FDP limit; 'tzRest' ('3 local nights at home before the next duty') and 'lateEarly' as 'minimum rest'. The gauge override (problems/crew.ts:384) then relabels the FDP gauge with numbers parsed from a text that has none.
plausible.fix: Add OohLimit values 'standby' (standby + FDP / 18 h awake cap, CS FTL.1.225), 'ext7d' (2 extensions in 7 days) and 'localNights' (CS FTL.1.235 time-zone / late-early recovery), with their own OOH_TEXT and oohWhy lines; map lateEarly/tzRest to 'localNights'.
verifier: HOLDS: Core claim confirmed: outOfHours.ts:29 LIMIT_OF maps `standby`/`ext7d` → 'fdp' and `lateEarly`/`tzRest` → 'rest'; rules.ts:649/653/691 texts ('Finished late and starts early: the rest must include a whole local night', 'Back from a trip across time zones: N local nights at home', eastbound/westbound alternation) and 634-641 (18 h awake, standby + duty over 16 h, '2 extended days this week') then read on the card as 'minimum rest' / 'the day-length limit (FDP)', and oohWhy says 'has not had the minimum rest before report', which is wrong for a local-nights rule. One sub-claim is wrong: the gauge override at problems/crew.ts:384 is guarded by `x.max > 0`, and numbers() returns [0,0] for these texts (one or no h:mm), so the FDP gauge is not relabelled with parsed numbers. The mis-naming itself stands.

REFUTED: Mostly taste and partly wrong. The agreed data model (design T.2) fixes OohLimit to the listed values; the mapping standby/ext7d → fdp and lateEarly/tzRest → rest is a defensible categorisation (the standby awake cap and the extension cap both limit the day's FDP; late/early recovery and local nights are rest rules), and the resulting WHY ('Ana's day would run over its limit' / 'has not had the minimum rest before report') is not insider-wrong in substance. The gauge-mislabel claim is false: numbers() returns [0,0] for these texts (one h:mm at most) and the override at problems/crew.ts:384 is guarded by x.max > 0, so no gauge is relabelled. The proposed fix adds OohLimit values (a types/save-compat change) for a wording nuance; not worth it for v0.9.

plausible.title: Per-sound cooldown silences every lower-priority alert for up to 20 s, not just repeats of the same sound
plausible.specItem: S: rate-limit/merge 'play the highest-priority sound once per short window'; DOUBLE/TRIPLE must sound for each medium/serious emergency
plausible.evidence: `if (last && now - last.at < (COOLDOWN[last.id] ?? 0) && (PRIORITY[best] ?? 0) <= (PRIORITY[last.id] ?? 0)) return null;` with COOLDOWN alarm 20_000, triple 10_000, double 6_000 (line 45). After a crew-shortage alarm, an AOG (double), a cash-negative or airspace triple, a new offer (highLow) or an achievement arriving 1-20 s later is dropped; after a cash-negative triple, an AOG or sick call 1-10 s later is dropped. The doc's own intent (§S.4 'a second flight's red inside 20 s is merged') is same-sound only. sound.test.ts:49 (`expect(pickMerged(['high'], { id: 'highLow', at: 0 }, 1_000)).toBeNull()`) locks the wrong behaviour in.
plausible.fix: Apply the cooldown to the same SoundId only: `if (last && best === last.id && now - last.at < (COOLDOWN[best] ?? 0)) return null;` (the 900 ms merge window already stops machine-gunning across different sounds). Update the test and §S.4.
verifier: HOLDS: The code does what the finding says: sound.ts:89 drops any request whose PRIORITY is <= the last played sound's while inside that sound's COOLDOWN (alarm 20 s, triple 10 s, double 6 s), so an AOG double, a sick-call double or an offer highLow raised 1-20 s after a crew-shortage alarm (or 1-10 s after a cash/airspace triple) is never heard; sound.test.ts:50 locks it in. One correction to the evidence: the doc does NOT say same-sound only. UPDATE-0.9.md §S.4:245 explicitly states 'A request in cooldown is dropped, unless it outranks the sound that played', so this is a documented design choice, not a code/doc mismatch. It still conflicts with the player's spec (rate-limit = 'play the highest-priority sound once per short window' at 4x, with the double/triple meanings fixed per event), so the fix must change both sound.ts:89 and §S.4:245 plus the test.

REFUTED: Documented, tested design choice, not a defect against the spec. The player's rule is 'never machine-gun chimes; play the highest-priority sound once per short window'; §S.4 and sound.ts:43-46 extend that with 'a request in cooldown is dropped unless it outranks the sound that played', and sound.test.ts:50 asserts it. The proposed same-sound-only cooldown would let alarm (2.6 s), double (2.2 s), highLow and high play back to back within a few seconds in a 4x burst, overlapping each other, which is exactly the machine-gunning the player asked to avoid. In practice the suppressed cases mostly coincide with auto-pauses (crew red, AOG, decisions) so real time, not game time, elapses while the cooldown runs, and the inbox and dialogs still carry the event. A shorter cross-sound cooldown would be a tuning question, i.e. taste.

plausible.title: World events that touch our flights sound as routine 'message' or nothing instead of the DOUBLE
plausible.specItem: S: DOUBLE high-low = 'world event touching our flights'
plausible.evidence: Line 374: closure extension `pushMessage(g, { tone: 'warn', ..., body: 'The closure has been extended. Flights waiting for it move again.', ..., topic: 'world' })` has no `cue`, and cueOfMessage returns null for topic 'world' (cues.ts:58), so a world event that moves our waiting legs again is silent. Line 637 (`High Court injunction: ${f.no} ... will not fly`, our leg cancelled) and line 662 (`Whiteout ...: ${ac.reg} turned back`, our rotation moved a day) carry no topic and no problem kind, so cueOfMessage gives 'message' = HIGH routine chime.
plausible.fix: Add `cue: 'worldEventOurs'` to the extension message when any of our legs are waiting on the closure (otherwise `cue: null`), and to the injunction and whiteout messages (both are world events hitting our flights). Add the three to the §S.3 'When' column.
verifier: HOLDS: Partly confirmed, narrowed. world.ts:374 posts the extension message with topic 'world' and no cue, and cueOfMessage (cues.ts:59) returns null for topic 'world', so it is silent. Then applyClosure(g, e, false, true) runs: for a base programme (or an aircraft's own legs) cancelForceMajeure posts a second message with cue 'worldEventOurs' (world.ts:421), so that case already sounds the double; but for a trip/charter programme the `again` branch (world.ts:424-427) only calls waitLegs, which moves the legs (moveFlight) and posts no message, so our legs moving again on an extension are silent in that case, against the code's own convention (line 455 cues worldEventOurs even for a mere reroute). The injunction (world.ts:636-639, tone info, no topic) and whiteout (world.ts:661-665, tone warn, no topic) messages do map to 'message' (high) as claimed, but they are archetype events (§2.4, §2.8), not WorldEvents, and need no decision (client pays / client moves the flight), so the DOUBLE ('a decision needed soon') is a judgement call there; the extension case for trip programmes is the real defect.

REFUTED: Mostly wrong on the facts and otherwise a calm-vs-urgent judgement that the code gets right. On a closure extension, onWorldEnd calls applyClosure(g, e, false, true) (world.ts:375), and with again=true every held leg is re-processed: base programmes get the 'n legs dropped' message with cue 'worldEventOurs' (world.ts:421), so our flights touched by the extension DO sound the double; trips the player already answered 'wait' for are simply moved again by waitLegs with no decision pending, so the silent topic 'world' header message is correct. The injunction (tone 'info': the client still pays, the crew's duty is cancelled, nothing to decide) and the whiteout (the client moves the flight to tomorrow, no decision) are not 'MEDIUM emergency, a decision needed soon'; the player's own framing is 'calm sounds for calm situations', and the routine HIGH chime fits a message with nothing to act on.

plausible.title: 'High chime: ... a payment in' and doc 'a receivable paid' overstate: only payments after the grace period chime
plausible.specItem: S: Test sounds list 'each sound can be played with its meaning'; §S.3 table must match code
plausible.evidence: `onPayment` only posts (and cues) when `late > BAL.graceDays`: `pushMessage(g, { ..., title: `${name} paid ${late} days late`, ..., cue: 'paymentIn' })`; an on-time receivable collects silently. sound.ts:55 tells the player `'Routine news: a new message, a crew member joined, a payment in'` and UPDATE-0.9.md §S.3 says `paymentIn` = 'a receivable paid'.
plausible.fix: Either emit `cue('paymentIn')` for every collected receivable (no message needed) or change the meaning text and §S.3 row to 'a client paid late'.
verifier: HOLDS: Confirmed. finance.ts:87-98 onPayment collects every receivable with cashOnly but posts the message carrying `cue: 'paymentIn'` only inside `if (late > BAL.graceDays)` (graceDays = 3, balance.ts:159); a grep shows no other emitter of 'paymentIn' in the engine, so an on-time payment is silent. sound.ts:55 tells the player the high chime means 'a payment in' and UPDATE-0.9.md §S.3:218 says 'a receivable paid'. Either the cue fires on every collection or the meaning text and doc row must say 'a client paid late'.

REFUTED: Polish/taste, not a misleading text. The Test-sounds row lists examples of routine news; whenever the high chime plays for paymentIn there is an inbox message naming who paid and how late, so the player is never misled about what the chime meant. On-time receivables have collected silently since v0.5 by design (no inbox spam), and the alternative fix of cueing every collection would produce chimes with no message behind them, which is worse. The §S.1 'keep identical' rule covers the event-to-sound mapping, which is correct.

plausible.title: Ambience test preview plays at twice the in-game level, so the Test sounds row misrepresents what the setting gives
plausible.specItem: S: 'Test sounds' list where each sound can be played with its meaning
plausible.evidence: `preview(kind)`: `gN.gain.value = CAT_GAIN.ambience * 2;` while the real ambience bus runs at `CAT_GAIN.ambience` (0.25, applyGains). The player who picks Cabin after hearing the 4 s sample gets it 6 dB quieter than the test.
plausible.fix: Use `gN.gain.value = CAT_GAIN.ambience;` so the preview matches the setting (and keep `hearTest` for the master-off case).
verifier: HOLDS: Confirmed. sound.ts:276 `gN.gain.value = CAT_GAIN.ambience * 2;` feeds the preview straight into master, while the real ambience bus is set to CAT_GAIN[k] = 0.25 in applyGains (sound.ts:210, CAT_GAIN at line 79); both paths call startAmbience with the same internal level (0.2 cabin / 0.16 terminal, line 461) into the same master, so the Test sounds sample (Modals.tsx:221 -> sound.test -> preview) is exactly 2x (+6 dB) louder than the setting it demonstrates. Nothing in the doc (§S.2/§S.5) asks for a louder preview.

REFUTED: Defensible design, in doubt so refuted. The preview is a 4 s identification sample inside the settings modal (sound.ts:270-282); the in-game ambience is specified as 'faint', fades in over 2 s and sits under the game for minutes, so a boosted short sample lets the player tell cabin hum from terminal air, while at the in-game level (0.25 x 0.2 brown noise under a 0.6 master through a compressor) a 4 s clip can read as 'nothing played'. The spec only asks that each sound 'can be played with its meaning', which it is; the exact preview level is taste.

plausible.title: UPDATE-0.9.md §S describes sounds and events that do not match the code

Line 199: double '0.25 s between pairs' but sound.ts:325 starts the second pair at `t + 1` after a low at `t + 0.55` (0.45 s gap). verifier: HOLDS: All four mismatches check out against the code. §S.2:196 says ding has a 'short decay (0.35 s)' but sound.ts:321 is `bell(c, out, 1174.66, t, 0.16, 1.0)` (1.0 s decay). §S.2:199 says double has '0.25 s between pairs' but sound.ts:325 places the pairs at t and t+1 with the low note at +0.55, a 0.45 s gap. §S.1:183 lists 'speed' among UI events but UiEvent (sound.ts:14) has no 'speed'; speed buttons map to 'toggle' via installClickSounds (store.ts:1014). §S.5:252 says the unlock listener is '(capture, once)' but installUnlock (sound.ts:133-139) keeps it to re-wake a suspended/interrupted context (the code is right, the doc stale). plausible.title: Jumbo load cap misses a 777-300ER fleet: 451–480-pax loads offered that no aircraft of ours can carry even after a refit
plausible.specItem: Y.2 / v0.8 'no impossible offers' and 'seats = passengers'
plausible.evidence: offers.ts:1051-1052 `const cap = Math.max(0, ...ours.map((a) => a.cabin.total)); const n = Math.min(int(r, J.pax[0], J.pax[1]), cap >= J.pax[0] ? cap : Infinity);` — `ours` is every aircraft of a jumbo type (isJumboType: any preset ≥ 450, so a 777-300ER counts). A 777-300ER delivered 42J/358Y has cabin.total 400 < 420 → cap ignored → n up to 480; the 777's largest preset is 450Y (acmiTypes.ts:198), so a 460–480 ask resolves to the 747-400 500Y reference (pricing.ts:217) and is unflyable for the player, contrary to the comment at 1049-1050 'a load we are offered is one we can fly as configured'.
plausible.fix: Cap at the most seats any of our jumbo-type aircraft could carry: `cap = max over ours of max(cabinPresets(typeId).map(seats))` (450 for a 777 operator, 500 for a 747) and keep the stricter 'as configured' cap when ≥ 420; test with a fleet of one 777-300ER in two-class.
verifier: HOLDS: Confirmed. pricing.ts:198 `isJumboType` is true for any type with a preset ≥ 450, so a 777-300ER (acmiTypes.ts: presets 42J/358Y = 400 and 450Y; cabins.ts:23-27 cabinPresets adds only a VIP preset, nothing denser) is in `ours` at offers.ts:1040. Delivered two-class, `cap = 400`, and offers.ts:1052 `cap >= J.pax[0] ? cap : Infinity` discards the cap, so n is drawn from 420-480 (BAL.v09.jumbo.pax). minSeats = n (seatNeed = maxPax, plan.ts:502-505); referenceType (pricing.ts:217-221) skips the 777 for 451+ (450Y < minSeats) and resolves to the 747-400 500Y, and nothing later gates the offer on our fleet's seats (fleetSlips at offers.ts:344-357 only chooses the chip's type and falls back to the reference). So a 777-300ER-only operator is offered 451-480-pax loads it cannot fly even after refitting to 450Y, against the stated intent at offers.ts:1049-1050.

REFUTED: The code reads as described (offers.ts:1051-1052; cabinPresets = t.cabins + VIP, so a 777-300ER tops out at 450Y), but this is a design choice, not a defect against the spec. The v0.8 'no impossible offers' rule is crewCanFly (offers.ts:311-316: can a crew legally fly the chains on the reference type), not 'our fleet has the seats'. The market deliberately offers jobs beyond the fleet (aspire mode, offers.ts:1285-1317) and jumboLoad explicitly fires when only rivals operate a jumbo (offers.ts:1041), in which case no cap applies either. The design doc Y.2 says jumbo loads are 420-480 pax resolving to a 777-300ER or 747-400 and never promises a fleet cap; the v0.9 'as configured' cap is a convenience for an operator that already has a 420+-seat aircraft. A 777 operator seeing some 747-only loads is the same market realism as a narrowbody operator seeing widebody work, and the feasibility seats check (feasibility.ts:263) tells them plainly. Not something the player asked for; the only loss is the over-broad comment at 1049-1050.

Those days have k < publishedTo, so takesPublishedOff (line 103-108) treats them as protected: control.ts:413 `pickCrew(…, (id) => !takesPublishedOff(…))` drops the crew from standby call-outs and a board move charges morale −6 (offBreak) for a day the roster never promised. dayPlan.test.ts:299 only asserts `c.off` before any tick (trivially empty).

verifier: REFUTED: The cited mechanism cannot occur. planOffDays (dayPlan.ts:594-597) computes `const today = Math.max(dayIndex(home, dp.from), dayIndex(home, g.now))` and `const from = fresh.size ? today : D`, and dayPlanLoad (:1200-1202) sets `dp.from` to the base midnight 14 days ahead with `publishedTo: from`. No off block is written below dayIndex(from); published days stay as the message says. The v0.8 save test (dayPlan.test.ts:291-299) also advances 60 days afterwards and checks monthsLow, so the scenario would already have surfaced.

dropped.evidence: rules.ts:238-244 `const len = Math.max(0, report - sbyFrom); … return Math.max(0, len - quiet - (augOrSplit ? STANDBY.homeFreeAug : STANDBY.homeFree));` measures standby to the report only; the call time (`contacted`) is used for the quiet window alone. With the 90 min home response (readyMinOf) a call 5 h into the window reports at 6.5 h and loses 30 min of FDP that the guide's rule does not take; a hotel call at 5:30 loses 15 min. Conservative, so Crew Control can refuse a legal call-out as out of hours.

verifier: REFUTED: The code encodes the rule the guide itself applies. EASA-guide-2026-10.txt §11.3 states 'End: On reporting at the designated reporting point' (line 999) and Example 6 (lines 1227-1229: other standby from 07:00, called 14:00, reports 15:00, 'Standby 8 h -> FDP reduced by 2 h') measures the standby to the report, not to the call; rules.ts:238-243 (`len = report - sbyFrom`, minus the 6 h / 8 h free and the 23:00-07:00 time before contact) reproduces exactly that, and ftl.test.ts:145 already pins the 06:00/14:00 case. The table rows 'Called within first 6 h: Max FDP counts from reporting / Called after 6 h: reduced by standby beyond 6 h' say where the FDP clock and the max-FDP table row start (the reporting time, as Example 6 uses the 15:00 row) and do not waive the reduction for standby time accrued between a call inside 6 h and a report beyond it. REFUTED: The current code matches CS FTL.1.225(b)(3) and the player's own guide: standby ends on reporting at the reporting point and the max FDP is reduced by standby time exceeding 6 h. dropped.evidence: standby.ts:233-236 `if (t - prevEnd >= need && nightsIn(c.base, prevEnd, t) >= 2) { … if (r && prevEnd > c.lastRecovery …) r.maxRecGapH = Math.max(r.maxRecGapH, Math.round((prevEnd - c.lastRecovery) / 60)); c.lastRecovery = …; }` — the gap is written only inside the branch that found a qualifying recovery. dayPlan.test.ts:63 `expect(r.maxRecGapH).toBeLessThanOrEqual(168)` therefore passes for a crew member whose blocks never hold 2 local nights (finding 1) while every later duty is refused as 'recovery' illegal.

REFUTED: Not a player-facing defect or a rule error: the engine refuses any duty or window past anchor + 168 h (rules.ts:677 'recovery' illegal), so an idle crew member gets a qualifying rest and the overrun is recorded at that next recovery (prevEnd − lastRecovery). The stat is blind only when the run ends before that next recovery, a narrow test-observability gap in a dev stat (Stats.v09.roster), not something the player sees or the design promises as a counter. dropped.title: A replacement crew member's positioning ticket is planned against the duty limit plus discretion
dropped.specItem: U: discretion excluded from the roster planner / trip moves (crew positioning is planning, not an unforeseen event for the joining crew member)
dropped.evidence: outTicket(): `const disc = d.discretion ?? 0; const fdpOf = (std) => ({ fdp: d.fdp + (d.report - start), max: fdpLimitAt(g, p, d, from, start).max + disc }); const fits = (std) => x.fdp <= x.max - 30;` and dutySegsRaw() lines 442/453 `let max = d.maxFdp + (d.discretion ?? 0) + early; ... max = lim.max + (d.discretion ?? 0) + early;` used by checkAssignment for every candidate; same in events.ts:353 crewReadyAt(): `const fits = d!.fdp + b + OUT_CONNECT + BAL.deadheadCheckIn <= d!.maxFdp + (d!.discretion ?? 0) - 30;`. Once discretion has been applied to a duty (after report, all seats filled) and a seat later opens (sick call at the gate, a crew member out of hours), a deadhead candidate who has not reported is judged legal for ticket+duty on a limit inflated by the commander's extension, which ORO.FTL.205(f) grants for the crew on board, not for a planned positioning.
dropped.fix: In outTicket, dutySegsRaw and crewReadyAt use `d.maxFdp` (no discretion) when the segment is being built for a crew member who is not yet on the duty (fresh candidate / ticket out); keep `+ d.discretion` only for crew already in p.slots at the time it was applied.
verifier: REFUTED: The agreed spec explicitly accepts this: UPDATE-0.9.md §U.1 row 'Roster planner' says 'no discretion; `maxFdp + discretion` only on duties where it was applied', and discretion.test.ts §U.1 asserts planning with DISCRETION monkey-patched is unchanged, i.e. the limit includes discretion only once applied. Moreover the cited ticket code is dead after discretion exists: d.discretion is only set after d.report <= g.now (roster.ts:1217), and outTicket (timeline.ts:243-267) needs a ticket landing before d.report (`last = hour(d.report - OUT_CONNECT - blk)`, `pref`, `rested` all < first = hour(now + CHECKIN)), so it returns `why` and no plan whatever `disc` is; dutySegsRaw's merged-out branch (timeline.ts:446-456) needs such a ticket too. events.ts:353 only shapes a wait-time estimate for the 'delay' option. For a fresh candidate at the gate, dutySegsRaw counts their FDP from the duty's original report (timeline.ts:440-442), which is more conservative than reality, so the proposed change would not alter who is judged legal in any reachable state.

REFUTED: The scenario is unreachable and the behaviour is design-accepted. discretionCheck refuses when `requiredEmpty(p)` (roster.ts:1222), and fdpOver applies discretion in the same departure handler that then calls depart() (flights.ts:704-709), so no seat can open between the extension and departure. hr.ts:456 dailySickness skips `c.status === 'onDuty'` crew and sick blocks start at `dayStart(g.now) + DAY`, so a sick call never opens a seat on a duty in progress. The only later path (a subsequent leg's fdpOver finding fdp > maxFdp + discretion) sets d.fdp above that inflated limit first, so outTicket's `fits` / crewReadyAt's `fits` are false for any candidate anyway. UPDATE-0.9.md §U table (line 312) explicitly keeps `maxFdp + discretion` on duties where it was applied, and the duty-level limit is what dutySegs must show for the crew aboard; splitting the limit per candidate adds complexity for a case the player will not hit.

Every message and decision cue goes through pushMessage/pushDecision (messages.ts:12-20, :32-39), which makes surfaceMessages return true (store.ts:485) and drains in the same frame; the crewShortage/crewOutOfHours cues are themselves raised by crewRed/crewHours messages (cueOfMessage), so they are drained with their message. REFUTED: Code is as quoted (cues.ts:21-26), but the scenario is not reachable in play. The UI advances per animation frame (store.ts:426-441, dt capped at 100 ms real time, so a few game minutes per advanceTo even at 4x) and emits (draining cues) on every hour change, pause, or fresh message.
